lockFileMaintenance.description: Refresh the lock files once a month, for review. Renovate runs weekly, so the first seven days of a month hold exactly one run. Cargo.lock gets its own PR through the rust-dependencies group. A refresh has no release timestamp, so minimumReleaseAge would hold it forever

customManagers.description: Tool versions pinned inside workflows (install-action tool inputs, env values, run text), each marked by a `# renovate:` comment on the line above. The github-actions manager reads only `uses:`

packageRules.description: Group and automerge non-major npm updates (devDependencies, pnpm overrides, packageManager)

Pin GitHub Actions digests; group and automerge non-major updates, digests included, once they are 3 days old: a retargeted tag is how the tj-actions/changed-files compromise spread. A digest update is aged by the release its tag resolves to but carries no timestamp of its own, which must not hold it forever

The tools pinned inside the workflows lint the workflows, fuzz the codecs or build what is released, so their updates are grouped and reviewed, never automerged. cargo-codspeed, which builds the benchmarks, follows the codspeed crates instead (next two rules)
prBodyNotes: A checksum next to a bumped version must be updated by hand in this PR: actionlint's `SHA256` in .github/workflows/ci.yml (from the release's checksums file) and the ziglang `--hash` in .github/workflows/build.yml (the SHA-256 of the release's x86_64 manylinux wheel on PyPI). CI fails until it is, through `sha256sum --check` and `pip3 install --require-hashes`.

shellcheck, wasm-pack and cargo-zigbuild install from the manifest of the pinned taiki-e/install-action, with no fallback. If an install step fails with `is not supported (updating install-action might resolve this)`, merge the pending github-actions update first, then rebase this PR.

packageRules.description: cargo-codspeed builds the benchmarks against the codspeed crates in Cargo.lock, so it moves with them in the rust-dependencies group

Automerge non-major cargo-codspeed updates, as the Rust crates are: a group automerges only when every update in it does, so without this rule cargo-codspeed would hold back the whole rust-dependencies PR. The codspeed crates already automerge on the same checks, and the CodSpeed job runs on that PR, since Cargo.lock changes

napi-rs toolchain: the CLI and the napi crates build and package every binary, so they update together and are reviewed, never automerged (#518, #526, #529). Keep this rule after the generic ones, as later rules win
Keep the napi-rs packages at exact versions in package.json, so a toolchain update shows in the reviewed diff and not only in pnpm-lock.yaml
Keep the typescript-5 alias on TypeScript 5: scripts/check-consumer-types.mjs type-checks the consumer projects with it as well as with the typescript devDependency

TypeScript compiles the JavaScript modules that npm publishes (scripts/build-js.mjs), and CI fails when their output changes. Update it in a pull request of its own, so that a release that changes the output, which then needs pnpm run build:js, holds up no other update

biome.json enables nursery rules, which a Biome release can rename or change, and pnpm run check fails on warnings. Keep Biome at an exact version, so that a new release arrives only in a pull request that runs the check with it, and update it in a pull request of its own, so that a release that needs pnpm exec biome migrate --write or new fixes holds up no other update
